short_description: Get hands-on with animals and explore a day in the life of a zookeeper!
meeting_point: 6461 El Apajo Rancho Santa Fe CA 92067
location_address: 6447 Helen Woodward Way Rancho Santa Fe, CA US 92067
description: This one-day camp involves unique hands-on activities from our professional animal care staff to give campers experiences with the different aspects of animal husbandry. This includes: diet preparation, animal exercise, enrichment strategies, training sessions, and more. Campers will be encouraged to follow their passion and explore their skills with animals of all kinds, such as large and small mammals, reptiles, and birds. Spots are extremely limited in order to provide the best and safest experience.
what_is_included:
* **Introduction to Exotic Pet Care:** Working with animals requires flexibility, patience, attentiveness and a strong work ethic. Our staff will explain and demonstrate how they care for more than 50 individual exotic pets.

* **Avians:** Some birds have strong personalities and bond with only a few people, while others befriend everyone they meet. Adapting your care and handling techniques for each individual animal is especially important when working with these feathered friends. Campers will find out how to successfully interact with birds, maintain enclosures and perches, and learn about proper nutrition.

* **Reptiles:** Do all animals eat every day? Could they possibly need daily cleaning and enrichment? Campers will discover the answer to those questions and practice feeding and handling different types of reptiles.

* **Small Mammals:** Rabbits, guinea pigs and chinchillas are absolutely adorable, but they do require a lot of care! They each have specific dietary needs that need to be followed carefully to ensure their health and well-being. The staff will show the group how to feed these cute critters.

* **Animal Training:** In fields like ours, training animals is about a lot more than just teaching behaviors that we think are “cute.” Animal caretakers utilize training to make sure that the animals can handle routine health procedures with reduced stress. Natural animal behaviors are shaped to be on cue to also have positive experiences with the staff and the public; it’s a great form of enrichment, too! Campers will have a blast practicing this crucial part of animal care and learning the fundamentals of training and how that varies depending on the species at hand.

* **Introduction to Barn Animal Care:** Just like the indoor animals, the barn animals that live outside need care and attention, too! The aspiring animal keepers will learn what it takes to maintain the health, cleanliness and enrichment for the lager species.

* **Sheep/Goats:** Hands-on careers like zookeepers or barn attendants may not always be glamorous, but they sure are rewarding! One of the first steps in the morning is cleaning enclosures, and campers will get to experience the satisfaction of a cleaning job well done. Exercise is an important part of proper animal care because it keeps the animals at a healthy weight and provides an outlet to burn energy.

* **Mini Horses:** Grooming is an important step of caring for animals because it allows for a physical inspection and routine handling that’ll help the animal be calm whenever medical treatments may be needed. Campers will get to practice grooming and exercising our miniature horses.

* **Closing Duties:** The staff will walk the campers through the end of day tasks that ensure our animals are safe and have what they need overnight. This includes checking food and water levels, general health and wellness, and securing enclosures. All good animal care industries have routine checks and procedures that help maintain animal health and safety.

highlight_title: Zookeeper Camp is an exciting chance to learn new skills with animals!
highlight_description: Zookeeper Camp gives kids in San Diego a behind-the-scenes experience with animal enrichment, diet prep, and hands-on learning alongside our animal ambassadors and professional care team.
check_in_details: You can wait by our lobby and when check-in begins a side gate will be opened. Staff with clipboards will be there to check you in 10 minutes prior to start time. Once checked in, parents are free to leave and campers will be directed to their class table to place down their items and get their nametag. Once check-in has finished the class Instructor will assemble all the campers to go over expectations, the schedule of the day, and begin!
what_to_bring:
* **Lunch**: Please pack lunches labeled with camper’s name. Lunches will be kept in the classroom. We do not have a refrigerator for campers and we do not have the ability to warm or cook lunches.
* **Snack**: Please let your child know what you have packed for snacks as opposed to lunch – otherwise some children will eat their entire lunch during snack time and have nothing left for lunch. Remember to label your child’s food.
* **Water bottle**: Please pack a water bottle and be sure to label it with your child’s first and last name. We have a filtered water dispenser for refills throughout the day.
* **Comfortable clothes**: Have your child dress in comfortable clothes that are ok to get dirty. Dress in layers as needed by weather.
* **Sunscreen**: Children are half indoors and half outdoors with shaded areas. If you choose, you may leave sunscreen labeled with your name so your child can reapply sunscreen mid-day. Please let your child’s teacher know.
* **Cell phones/cameras**: Phones, cameras, and tablets may be brought. Your child can use them when instructed to help capture your child's experience, but only photos of the animals/activities can occur. Not all parents authorize pictures to be taken of their child. Please be mindful children are responsible for the items they bring.
special_requirements:
* If your child has an aide at school and you plan to have them attend with your child, or if you need to attend with your child, please call us at 858-756-4117 ext. 406 so that we can help them complete the fingerprint process. All aides MUST complete fingerprinting in order to attend and this process includes a livescan fee (paid to the livescan facility) and can take days or weeks to get results back.
* **Medication**: We must have a signed medical authorization release in order to give any medications to campers, which you can fill out during check-in and drop off any medication with the staff if it's needed by your child. Medications will be safely stored in the office. Please remember to pick them up at check-out.
* **Late fee policy**: Camp ends at 3:00pm. If your child(ren) are not picked up by 3:20pm you will be charged a late fee of $15 per camper, every 15 minutes.
 * **Transfer policy**: With 24 hours or more weekday notice we can transfer registrations which haven't started to another day, if that day has room, for the same camp, for any purpose.
* **Sick policy**: Communicate with us about child illness and we can discuss cancellation policy allowances. Please keep sick children home. Camp adheres to CDC guidelines.
* **Discipline policy**: Our camp staff are well trained and expected to resolve behavior issues in a positive manner. Our goal is to provide every child with a rewarding camp experience. At the beginning of the camp day, the camp teacher goes over camp rules. In the event that a rule is broken, the teacher gives the class a reminder. If the same child breaks a rule again, a verbal reminder directed at that child is issued including stating the problem and a solution. If a rule is broken again, the teacher will send the child to the office to think about the problem and discuss the problem/solution with the camp leadership. The camp leadership will call home to discuss behavior and a solution plan. Examples of behavior that will result in a camper being immediately asked to leave camp include, but are not limited to: destruction of property or disruptive behavior which threatens the safety of other campers, animals, volunteers, or staff. In such a case, camp fees are non-transferable and non-refundable.
restrictions:
* This camp is for kids only! Must be 9 or older for safety and maturity reasons with the activities and level of knowledge we provide.
* All campers must be able to use the restroom confidently and on their own.
* **Shoes**: For safety reasons, closed-toed shoes only. No sandals allowed.
* **Drawstrings**: For safety reasons, drawstrings (hoodies, pants or shorts) should not be worn on the playground.
* **Pets**: No pets are allowed on the campgrounds. There are no exceptions to this safety policy. Cannot leave pets alone in vehicles.
* **Toys, books, stuffed animals, etc.**: These may get soiled, broken, or lost—best to leave at home.
* **Sharp objects**: For safety purposes please leave anything that is a sharp or hazardous at home.

faqs:
**Why is this priced higher than your other Camps?**
In order to give campers the best and most hands-on experience we have to strictly limit the maximum capacity of this program, therefore each available slot costs a bit more when compared to other programs. However this means your camper is getting a lot more direct and longer term interaction with our animals. No other program we offer gets you this behind scenes and up close and personal with the animals here!

**The camp is offered several times a year, is each one different?**
We run the same style of program on each date so they aren't designed to be different, but when working with animals you should always expect the unexpected so you might end up with a greater focus with certain animals, or do slightly different things with them, than the time you attended before.

**My child wants to work with animals, should they become a veterinarian?**
Veterinarian is often the first career we think of when it comes to working with animals, and it can be the perfect career for some people. However pursuing the career is difficult, can be expensive, and might not be what everyone is looking for. There are a lot of ways you can work directly with animals, or indirectly support them. We discuss this at our career camps so join us to find out more!

**Authorized Pick Up & ID Checking**
For safety purposes we do not release children at pick up time to anyone not listed on the “authorized to pick up” list. We check ID daily at checkout time. To add someone to the authorized list, we must confirm you are one of the parents/guardians and then we can add any additional names, or you can log into your account and add more in yourself.
